articles.content_html:
C’è poi un’altra cosa per cui il Post è diverso da altri giornali e altri progetti di informazione: la maggior parte degli articoli non è firmata. Abbiamo fatto questa scelta per fare prevalere le informazioni, i fatti, i dati, rispetto allo stile e alle valutazioni personali. E anche perché gli articoli del Post sono molto spesso frutto di un lavoro collettivo che non sarebbe opportuno ricondurre alle singole persone.

Funziona questo approccio? Per il momento ci ha permesso di costruire un rapporto di complicità con lettrici e lettori e, grazie agli abbonamenti, anche di dimostrare che un giornalismo diverso, basato sulla fiducia, può essere economicamente sostenibile. Anche in tempi bui per i giornali di tutto il mondo. Questo perché ci sono persone pronte a pagare affinché chiunque, anche chi non può permettersi un abbonamento, abbia accesso a un’informazione di qualità. Se è un’idea che ti piace, puoi dare una mano anche tu.

articles.content_html: SK Hynix is in exploratory talks with Intel over a deal that would have it manufacture memory chips in the US for the first time, with one scenario having it lease part of Intel's long-delayed Ohio campus and another forming a joint venture with Intel and major cloud providers to lock in steady memory supply. articles.content_html: Figure pretrained Helix 2.5 entirely on Index, its crowdsourced human video dataset, then fine-tuned three whole-body behaviors - tidying rooms, folding towels, making beds - before deploying a single fixed checkpoint into 30 Bay Area homes it had never seen, with no data collection or adaptation on-site and objects it had never encountered. The key isolation test: training two otherwise identical policies on the same task-specific data, one from random initialization and one from Index-pretrained weights, showed Index pretraining alone lifted zero-shot success from 9% to 56%, over 6x higher, with success requiring full task completion and no partial credit.

articles.content_html: Mixture-of-Experts models keep growing capacity by adding more experts, but even after quantization, the full expert pool still dwarfs consumer RAM and VRAM, so local inference has to lean on SSD storage instead - a much harder problem than just having enough disk space. SSD-LLaMA builds an SSD I/O pipeline tuned specifically for fetching experts, layered with a three-tier SSD-RAM-VRAM hierarchy that dynamically decides which experts to hold where, and CPU-GPU hybrid execution balanced against the SSD's limited bandwidth, all while running every selected expert in full rather than pruning or substituting cheaper approximations.

articles.title: Invisible changes to a robot's training world can make it fail in real life (3 minute read)
articles.summary: Every 3D asset in a robot simulator carries two geometries - a visual mesh for rendering and a coarser collision mesh for physics - a legitimate gap since matching them exactly is too expensive. This paper shows that gap is exploitable: an attacker can alter only the collision mesh, so a policy trained on the poisoned asset looks and behaves normally in simulation, then fails or creates real...
articles.content_html: Every 3D asset in a robot simulator carries two geometries - a visual mesh for rendering and a coarser collision mesh for physics - a legitimate gap since matching them exactly is too expensive. This paper shows that gap is exploitable: an attacker can alter only the collision mesh, so a policy trained on the poisoned asset looks and behaves normally in simulation, then fails or creates real safety risks once deployed. It slips past existing checks entirely, since asset review covers malware, copyright, and format, but nothing verifies visual-collision consistency, and the researchers found the defenses they tested weren't enough to catch it.

articles.content_html: Delos Data, founded by Intel veterans, raised $100 million led by Matrix Partners and Playground to build networking chips and software that move data faster between processors inside increasingly heterogeneous AI data centers. Early AI data centers were mostly Nvidia GPUs wired together with Nvidia's own proprietary networking, but as the focus has shifted from training toward running persistent, failure-tolerant agentic inference workloads, data centers now mix GPUs, XPUs, accelerators, CPUs, memory, and storage from Nvidia, AMD, Cerebras, and others, none of which were designed to talk to each other efficiently at that scale.

articles.content_html: An unverified Geekbench 7 result for Apple's new 2nm M6 chip, debuting in the new Mac mini, shows a single-core score of 4,071 and a multi-core score of 22,783, up roughly 12% and 27% respectively over the M5's average scores. articles.content_html: HubSpot spent twelve months testing what gets a company found in AI search.
